rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation changes comparison from '>' to '>='. This affects which index is stored when duplicate max values exist (first vs last occurrence), but the max VALUE itself is always identical. Since return_indices=False is hardcoded in forward(), indices are never returned. Output tensor contains only max values, which are bitwise identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation at line 58 changes when max_index is updated - the original selects the first occurrence of the maximum, while the mutant selects the last occurrence when duplicates exist. However, the computed maximum value (max_val) is always identical regardless of which comparison operator is used. The forward() method hardcodes return_indices=False, so only the output tensor containing max values is returned. Since indices are never exposed in the output, the behavioral difference caused by the mutation cannot be observed through any input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The mutation only affects index selection, but indices are not returned (return_indices=False). To kill this mutant would require changing the forward() method to pass return_indices=True, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing max pooling kernels, ensure test coverage includes scenarios where return_indices=True to verify index correctness. The current test configuration only validates max values, leaving index computation untested against comparison operator mutations.
